Indicator 7b compares the pass rates for the Danish public school leaving examination (*folkeskolens afgangseksamen*) among youth in the [[adhd-behandlingspopulation|ADHD-behandlingspopulation]] against a general benchmark, the [[baggrundspopulationen-2023|Baggrundspopulationen 2023]], across five Danish regions. The data reveals a persistent and significant achievement gap: while the background population consistently achieves pass rates between 81% and 87%, the ADHD treatment population's rates range from 49% to 81% depending on the specific metric and reporting year [^src1] [^src2].

Across both the 2023 and 2024 reports, [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] consistently emerges as the leader among the regions for the ADHD treatment population. In the 2023 report, it recorded a pass rate of 73% (97/132) in the primary metric [^src1], and in the 2024 report, it maintained the lead with 69% (270/389) [^src2]. Conversely, the trailing regions shifted slightly: [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] recorded the lowest primary pass rate in the 2023 report at 61% (69/113) [^src1], while [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] fell to the bottom in the 2024 report with a pass rate of just 49% (98/199) [^src2].

When examining trends between the two reports, the national pass rate for the primary metric in the ADHD treatment population decreased from 65% (519/799) in the 2023 data [^src1] to 58% (948/1644) in the 2024 data [^src2]. Meanwhile, a secondary metric (the middle "Andel" column) shows the national rate holding relatively steady at 67% in both reports [^src1] [^src2]. The background population's pass rate also saw a slight decline at the national level, dropping from 86% (60,247/70,411) in the 2023 report [^src1] to 84% (58,615/70,070) in the 2024 report [^src2], indicating that while the gap remains wide, the benchmark itself is not entirely static. Notably, [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] experienced a sharp drop in the background population pass rate from 84% in 2023 [^src1] to 81% in 2024 [^src2], making it an outlier on the lower end of the benchmark spectrum in the more recent data.

Beyond the specific findings for Indicator 7b, the full 2023 and 2024 reports provide extensive additional context, methodologies, and analyses of other indicators across their remaining sections [^src3] [^src14] [^src17] for the 2023 publication, and [^src4] [^src5] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8] [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12] [^src13] [^src15] [^src16] for the 2024 edition.
